newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times Jan 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- MILITARY SPENDING RISE SPURRED BOEING BID

In an interview with the Financial Times, Philip Condit, chief executive of aerospace giant Boeing, revealed that the company launched its takeover of McDonnell Douglas because it believed US defence spending would begin to grow again and it wanted a larger military business to take advantage of this. Condit is confident the takeover will win regulatory approval because it is in line with US policy of promoting defence industry mergers.
-- CITY FACES BLOW OVER EU PLANS FOR TAKEOVER RULES

The City of London is bracing itself for a wave of litigation if a European Union directive is approved by a key committee of the European Parliament. The compulsory directive on company takeovers and mergers is being bitterly opposed by UK regulatory authorities, who fear the imposition of a statutory regime in place of the City's voluntary system could lead to compensation claims in excess of 1 billion stg.
-- ECONOMY BOOSTS TORY POLL HOPES

A series of reports have predicted accelerated growth for the economy and rising consumer demand, boosting hopes among Conservatives that the party will approach the general election on the back of a visible economic recovery. But the reports, from Lloyds Bank, Oxford Economic Forecasting and Cambridge Econometrics, also warn that the next government may have to raise taxes and interest rates soon after taking office in order to cool buoyant consumer demand.
-- BIG OUTLAY ON DIGITAL TELEVISION IMMINENT

The UK cable industry is expected to decide within the next two months whether to invest several hundred million pounds in producing decoders to enable Britain's 1.7 million cable customers to receive digital cable television services. A working party representing the UK's large cable companies has already agreed a common standard for the digital decoders, and the group's chairman, Derek Lewis of the UK Gold channel, says he expects a decision on investment in the next two months.
-- BETTER REDUNDANCY ADVICE FOR OLDER PEOPLE URGED

The Carnegie Third Age Programme, a group which campaigns for better opportunities for older people, has warned that employees are suffering from a lack of advice and support when they are made redundant. The programme has called for a series of measures for older workers made jobless, including independent financial advice, support for job-seeking efforts, and advice on welfare benefits.
-- POWER NETWORKS BRACED FOR SURGE

The National Grid and British Gas TransCo, the two companies responsible for Britain's electricity and natural gas networks, are closely monitoring any increase in demand for power as industries return to work during the current cold snap. The energy supply companies are preparing for any surge in demand, and TransCo has already moved to cut off some 'interruptible' contracts in areas of the south-west to ensure adequate supplies are available to remote areas.
-- MERRILL SET TO LEAD MATAV OFFERING

US investment bank Merrill Lynch is expected to be named as the lead bank in the flotation of Hungarian national telecoms company Matav. The issue will be eastern Europe's largest equity offering, possibly reaching as much as $1 billion. The appointment of Merrill is expected to be announced later this month.
-- GREENWICH LISTING REQUEST IS REJECTED

Greenwich Communications, the loss-making UK supplier of satellite receiving equipment in Portugal, has failed in its bid to join the London Stock Exchange. Greenwich, which is 40 per cent owned by investment trust Gresham House, was told it had been refused because it did not meet Stock Exchange's listing requirements 'by virtue of their business'.
-- COMPUTING SECTOR FAVOURS NASDAQ

UK companies specialising in software products or computing services are increasingly favouring the Nasdaq electronic stock market for listings. The latest monthy review of the UK computing services industry in the publication System House reveals that last year as many UK companies in the sector chose to float on Nasdaq as on UK exchanges.
-- SAMSUNG ABANDONS ATTEMPT TO BUY FOKKER

South Korean aerospace company Samsung has abandoned its bid to take over Fokker, the bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker. The deal collapsed after Samsung failed to secure financial support for the Fokker acquisition from other Korean aerospace companies under a government-sponsored plan. The Russian aircraft maker Yakovlev is now thought to be the only company still interested in Fokker.
